text: SunPass is an electronic toll collection system in Florida, United States, created in 1999 by the Florida Department of Transportation's (FDOT's) Office of Toll Operations, operating as a division of Florida's Turnpike Enterprise (FTE). The system uses windshield-mounted RFID transponders manufactured by TransCore and lane equipment designed by TransCore, SAIC, and Raytheon. It was introduced on April 24, 1999, and by October 1 of that year, over 100,000 SunPass transponders had been sold. In early 2009, all Easy Pay customers automatically became SunPass Plus customers if they opted in to use their transponders for airport parking at Tampa, Orlando, Palm Beach, Fort Lauderdale, and Miami airports, with the option to opt out. The SunPass Mini was introduced on July 1, 2008, and became available at retail locations; it is a passive RFID transponder about the size of a credit card, requiring no batteries, and must be mounted on a glass windshield to function properly, with removal damaging the pass; it does not work on motorcycle windshields. SunPass Portable (or SunPass Pro) transponders can be transferred between vehicles. SunPass-only toll lanes on most Florida toll roads allow vehicles to pass at speeds up to 25 mph (40 km/h) for safety, while the Turnpike uses all-electronic tolling (AET) and toll by plate for highway speeds, with mainline toll barriers having dedicated lanes for full-speed automatic toll collection up to 65 mph (105 km/h). In September 2010, February 2011, April 2014, and June 2014, Florida's Turnpike Enterprise converted the Homestead Extension of Florida's Turnpike, the Sawgrass Expressway, the Veterans Expressway, and the Veterans Expressway to open road tolling using SunPass, ending cash collection; motorists without a SunPass are billed via toll by plate, which uses cameras and sends a bill to the registered vehicle owner including a toll and administrative fee; failure to pay results in a $100 fine plus tolls owed, with possible court costs, license points, license suspension, or registration suspension. SunPass is fully interoperable with E-Pass (Central Florida Expressway Authority), O-Pass (Osceola County, now folded into E-Pass), LeeWay (Lee County toll bridges), and Miami-Dade Expressway Authority (MDX) toll roads. Initially, SunPass was not compatible with out-of-state systems; the federal Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act (MAP-21), adopted in July 2012, required all toll facilities to be interoperable by October 1, 2016. SunPass announced in 2012 plans to become interoperable with E-ZPass; by the end of 2015, older battery-powered transponders were phased out, and new batteryless models support out-of-state tolling. On July 29, 2013, Florida's Turnpike Enterprise entered into an interoperability agreement with North Carolina Turnpike Authority and NC Quick Pass, allowing SunPass holders to use North Carolina toll roads and lanes. On November 12, 2014, an interoperability agreement was made with Georgia's Peach Pass, enabling SunPass use on I-85 Express lanes and future toll roads or lanes in Georgia. The C-Pass system on the Rickenbacker and Venetian Causeways was replaced by SunPass and pay-by-plate on September 23, 2014. In July 2020, E-ZPass announced SunPass would be compatible with E-ZPass by the end of 2020 and Peach Pass in 2021; on May 28, 2021, Florida Turnpike Enterprise began accepting E-ZPass, and E-ZPass facilities began accepting SunPass Pro transponders, but not earlier models like SunPass Portable or SunPass Mini. On February 27, 2023, SunPass was announced as compatible with toll roads in Kansas and Oklahoma and certain toll roads in Texas, supporting both SunPass Mini and SunPass Pro transponders; however, transponders from Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas cannot be used on any tolled roads maintained by the Central Florida Expressway Authority. In March 2025, the Harris County Toll Road Authority reached an interoperability agreement with Florida Turnpike Enterprise, making SunPass accepted statewide in Texas, with EZ Tag and TxTag accepted on all Florida Turnpike Enterprise roads. In November 2025, the E-470 Public Highway Authority reached an interoperability agreement with Florida Turnpike Enterprise, allowing SunPass use on E-470 and the express lanes network in Colorado, and ExpressToll acceptance on all Florida Turnpike Enterprise roads.
